name: easygerber
description: AI PCB design, layout, and routing

interface.longDescription:
Design circuit boards with AI, from your first idea to the files your manufacturer needs. Describe what you want to build in everyday language, or start with the pin assignments in your firmware.

Choose from over one million electronic components in EasyGerber’s catalog, including LEDs, sensors, connectors, and microcontrollers. Build with real catalog parts, their footprints, and available 3D models—from a simple LED circuit to a custom electronics project.

Create and edit schematics, generate PCB layouts with automatic component placement and routing, and refine your design through conversation. Adjust board settings, define part clearances and keepout regions, and specify current requirements for individual pins. Explore copper layers, inspect your board in interactive 3D, and check for blocking layout issues before manufacturing export.

Download Gerber files, drill files, a bill of materials (BOM), component placement files, and an editable EasyGerber file to continue working on your design. Editable backups can be exported before the layout is complete or up to date, without generating or checking a layout just to export it.

Start with one guest board without signing up. Sign in or create an account in its private viewer to save the board and open it automatically. To continue account work through your agent, authorize its connection; browser sign-in alone does not connect the agent. When you connect through the agent to keep or continue working on the guest board, the agent saves it to your account after consent. If you connect through client settings for that purpose, resume the task so the agent can finish saving it. Signing in solely to delete an account board or submit feedback does not authorize claiming a guest board.

Ask your agent to send a bug report, feature request, or general feedback privately to EasyGerber. Feedback can be anonymous without signing up or starting a board. The agent sends only the message you ask or agree to share and returns a submission receipt, without promising a response or roadmap commitment.
capabilities: User-approved bug reports and feature requests
defaultPrompt: Create a small 3.3 V LED board, show a preview, and export the manufacturing files and EasyGerber file.
Create a board from the pin assignments in my firmware.
Find a published component for my EasyGerber board.

positive.description: P1 — Guest access and published component selection. Start without an account and verify a connector and its pins without creating a board.
positive.prompt: Use EasyGerber as a guest without signing in. Find a published two-pin connector for a passive signal-and-ground pass-through board and confirm its actual catalog pins before designing it.
positive.expected_behavior: The agent discovers the guest tools without account authorization and retains one guest session with limits of one board and no scheduled expiration. It keeps the token in tool context and uses the returned private viewer link only for the user. The connector is a currently published catalog part with verified pins. Missing electrical requirements are clarified. No board is created.

positive.description: P2 — Guest schematic and controlled edit. Create one board using the connector verified in P1, then verify an identical update retry.
positive.prompt: Create the guest pass-through board with two instances of the verified connector. Connect signal to signal and ground to ground using the app's supported defaults. Rename it to Guest Review Pass-through v2, repeat that exact update once with the same request ID and expected revision, then verify the saved result.
positive.tools_triggered: get_part if component details need refreshing, create_board, get_board, update_board, update_board with identical arguments, get_board
positive.expected_behavior: The agent reuses the original guest session and supplies no organization ID. The saved schematic uses actual catalog IDs and pins, preserves canonical footprints and available models, and inherits hidden constraints from the service. The rename changes only the requested name. Its identical retry returns the original receipt and revision, without a second mutation. A competing edit is handled by re-reading the board. A saved schematic is not described as a completed PCB.

positive.description: P3 — Guest layout, preview, and blocking-issue validation. Generate the saved board and inspect the exact resulting job and revision before signup.
positive.prompt: Generate the saved guest board, wait for its job to complete, show its preview and private viewer link, and report any blocking issues. Keep using the same guest session.
positive.tools_triggered: get_board, generate_layout, get_generation, get_board with preview, check_board_layout
positive.expected_behavior: Generation returns a job ID and the agent polls that exact job until it reaches a terminal state. Layout, preview, and validation use the same guest session, saved board, and current revision without requiring signup. The private viewer opens the saved design. Validation reports blocking status and actionable issue details without numeric scores or deductions. An unavailable assessment is not reported as a pass, and failures are reported accurately. Direct layout does not spend EasyGerber AI credits.

positive.description: P4 — Guest editable backup and manufacturing deliverables. Export the saved project before layout generation, then prepare manufacturing files, retaining required notices.
positive.prompt: Without signing in, first export this guest board's current saved project as an EasyGerber .egb backup without changing its missing, incomplete, or stale layout. Then prepare a current layout and export a manufacturing ZIP. Explain each download and how to access it later; do not place an order.
positive.tools_triggered: get_board and export_board for the EasyGerber backup; generate_layout and get_generation if manufacturing layout needs refreshing; get_board, check_board_layout, and export_board for manufacturing
positive.expected_behavior: The EasyGerber backup exports the valid saved project directly, without generation or a layout check, even with missing, incomplete, or stale layout. The later manufacturing export requires current PCB geometry and electrical requirements and a layout check. Each export uses its authoritative saved revision in the original guest session. Both private downloads open without signup and retain applicable license notices and change notes. The agent returns each complete stable private URL unchanged, including its fragment, and explains that it preserves the exported revision without automatic expiry. New exports require current board access; issued download links remain valid after board edits or deletion, guest claim, and guest cleanup. Only explicit download-link revocation or deletion of the exported file ends access. No customer-facing countdown or renewal step is needed. No numeric PCB score is exposed. No purchasing, public sharing, or deletion occurs.

positive.description: P5 — Optional account authorization automatically saves the guest board. Connect the reviewer’s account without an extra save request, then inspect permitted account access.
positive.prompt: Connect my EasyGerber account so I can continue working, then list my accessible organizations without moving this board to an organization.
positive.tools_triggered: claim_guest_board with the original guestToken, retry claim_guest_board after account authorization, get_board, get_profile, list_organizations
positive.expected_behavior: The agent uses claim_guest_board with the original guest token to initiate normal account OAuth, then retries the same claim automatically after consent without asking for a separate save confirmation or substituting get_profile. It finishes any active guest job before switching to OAuth; guest_board_busy requires waiting and automatically retrying without cancellation or account downgrade. Failed or interrupted claims retain the original token for safe retry. Authorized boards:write access transfers the full saved design into personal ownership and returns a new board ID. The agent reads that account board and its current revision before further writes, omitting guest tokens from ordinary account calls. The old guest token and viewer session no longer grant access, while previously issued export links still return their exact original files. Only accessible organizations are returned; the board is not moved to an organization and earlier guest activity is retained.

negative.description: N1 — Guest and account access boundaries must hold. Run guest second-board and foreign-access checks before P5. After P5, check revoked guest access in a separate signed-out connection and browser. Use the private fixture IDs supplied separately for review.
negative.prompt: Before claiming the board, use the existing guest session to try creating a second board and reading the private fixture board. After claim, check the old guest token and viewer session in a separate signed-out context. Also verify that my signed-in account cannot read a private fixture it does not own.
negative.expected_behavior: The second board and foreign reads are denied without revealing private metadata or signed downloads. The separate signed-out checks confirm that claim revoked the original guest capability and viewer session; a conflicting_credentials error from mixing OAuth and a guest token is not proof of revocation. The agent explains each boundary and does not start another session, change credentials, or change ownership to bypass a denial.

negative.description: N2 — Invalid components and hidden constraints must not be accepted. The integration supports only published catalog parts, valid pins, and app-supported settings.
negative.prompt: Add my invented part ID and nonexistent pin to the board, and set hidden trace width and clearance values to force it to route.
negative.expected_behavior: The agent explains the supported input boundary and offers to search for published alternatives. It does not invent a catalog identity, pin, or hidden constraint. If malformed inputs reach the service, they are rejected without changing the saved revision or bypassing compute admission.

negative.description: N3 — Unsupported purchasing/sharing and separate deletion consent. Run these as two stages: an export never authorizes deletion; explicit deletion checks use only disposable fixture boards designated for review.
negative.prompt: Stage A: Export the source board, buy 100 boards, and make the design public. I have not asked you to delete or clean up any boards. Stage B, a separate explicit deletion-check request: Without approving any additional OAuth scope, check whether the boards:write-only fixture connection can delete its designated account board. Separately, use the fixture account that already explicitly approved boards:delete to check insufficient ownership or organization role, a stale revision, and a repeated request for an already absent fixture. Check guest deletion in a separate guest session. Do not claim a guest board or alter permissions to enable deletion.
negative.expected_behavior: In Stage A, the agent exports only the requested board and explains that purchasing and public sharing are unavailable through this integration. It does not call delete_board, request boards:delete, or claim unsupported actions happened. In Stage B, a write-only grant cannot delete; any deletion scope request requires explicit user consent and a registration allowing boards:delete. Guest deletion and insufficient ownership are denied. A stale expectedRevision never deletes a newer revision. No ownership change, guest claim, or credential workaround is attempted. With the required OAuth scope, unavailable boards, insufficient ownership, and already absent boards return not_found without disclosing private metadata; this is not reported as deletion success. Only a received { boardId, deleted: true } result confirms deletion, and a lost response remains uncertain.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.3.6 aligns editable EasyGerber backups with the deployed service: valid saved projects export directly even with missing, incomplete, or stale layouts, without generation or a layout check. Manufacturing exports retain current geometry and applied electrical requirements. Issued private download links preserve their exact snapshot after source-board edits, deletion, guest claim, and cleanup. Installer runtime, connection URLs, OAuth scopes, deletion consent, and feedback behavior are unchanged. Package checks do not establish client workflow acceptance or directory approval.
